**Roadmap:** `doc/roadmap/bus-balance-blueprint.md` (revision 3, 2026-09-14, amended 2026-09-15 after the Layer 0 review, 2026-09-18 after the Layer 1 review and 2026-09-21 after the review of the Layer 1 follow-ups, and 2026-09-23 after the reading audit and the adversarial review of Layer 3; it carries a review record for each) — the specification of what is wanted; changed only by pull request; never records status. From 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-24 it rode on the Clean PR branch, with the status file and the review records, in safekeeping commits; those commits were dropped from #464 on 2026-09-24 (the branch history was rewritten; the files are kept locally, outside the pull request); it is to be added under [`docs/roadmap/`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/leanerVM/tree/main/docs/roadmap) here by pull request, since this repository owns the requirement (#16).
**Status:** `doc/roadmap/bus-balance-status.md` — where it stands; rewritten whole when a layer lands. Same home as the roadmap.
**Code:** Clean draft pull request [Verified-zkEVM/clean#464](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/pull/464), from branch `feat/bus-balance-binary-fields` on the `scaraven` fork, based on `93c9d1ef` (Lean and Mathlib `v4.33.1`, the pin leanerVM uses). The one pull request carries every layer, one review unit per layer (Layer 1 is six commits: three for the layer and three review follow-ups; Layer 3 is five: four for the layer and one review follow-up; Layer 4 is three: the layer, its review follow-up and the Fibonacci example that replaced its counter VM), followed by one comment-only commit that brings every file of the change to the library's commenting style, and is reviewed one layer per pass. Head after the 2026-09-24 push: [`a1938ad5`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/a1938ad5).

Until the two documents are published, this issue carries their content in summary; once they are, it holds nothing that is not in them, and where they disagree, the files win.

Related: #16 (the request this plan answers: direction as data, balance counted in `ℕ`, ensemble theorems without `[Fact (ringChar F ≠ 2)]`); #4 (leanISA dashboard: Layers 9 and 10 consume the result; Layer 5's `Direction`/`channelDir` and Layer 8's `BalancedPair` are the workarounds it retires); #12 (the proof-system roadmap reads the M3 bus off the same channels). Upstream: Clean [#452](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/issues/452) (capacity bound; the side-condition half of #16's item 2), Clean [#446](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/pull/446) (independent). Downstream: sp1-lean pins Clean `292b9cc3` and its reader proofs supply two premises to every channel requirement with `fun _ _ => …`; that shape must keep compiling.

## What this roadmap builds

Clean's bus has two boundaries. The **channel operations** fix the local proof contract of one row: what a row that receives a message may assume about it, and what a row that provides a message must prove. The **balance argument** connects the rows: it justifies, from the verifier's per-channel relation, that every assumption made locally was established by some provider. Over `K = GF(2^64)` both fail today, because Clean reads direction off the sign of the multiplicity (`-1 = 1`) and defines balance as a field sum guarded by `length < ringChar F` (`= 2`). The failure is in the local contract as much as in the balance predicate: changing only `BalancedInteractions` does not repair a `push` requirement that is `True` at multiplicity `1`.

The plan adds an **opt-in directed path** beside the legacy one and changes no legacy statement:

| Boundary | Legacy (unchanged) | Directed (new, opt-in) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Channel | `Channel`, `Channel.toRaw`, `emit/push/pull/pushIf/pullIf`; direction is the sign of the multiplicity | `DirectedChannel`, `DirectedChannel.emit dir enabled msg / push / pushIf / pull / pullIf`; direction is a **tag stored as the last raw message element** (`Direction.tag`: `0` provide, `1` receive), the multiplicity is a boolean activation gate |
| Local contract | `Requirements := mult ≠ -1 → mult ≠ 0 → G`; `Guarantees := mult = -1 → G` | an active provider owes `G` and a boolean gate; an active receiver may assume `G` (`pullIf`) or decline it (`emit .receive`); a disabled event owes and assumes nothing; a raw interaction whose last element is neither tag fails the requirements |
| Balance | `BalancedInteractions` = field sum + no-wrap guard, read through `Interaction.legacyEvent` | `BalanceModel.multiset` = the active provided payloads are a permutation of the active received payloads, read through `Interaction.directedEvent`; no characteristic condition |
| Kernel | `guarantees_of_requirements_of_requirements_of_guarantees` with `[Fact (ringChar F ≠ 2)]` (kept, now a wrapper) | `Event`, `PullsSupported`, `CountBalanced` over `ℕ` counts, parametrized by the reading; `guarantees_of_requirements_of_count_eq` with no field at all |
| Ensemble | `Statement`, `FormalEnsemble`, builders | `BalanceModel`, `Ensemble.StatementWith model`, `SoundnessWith`, `CompletenessWith`, `FormalEnsembleWith`; **no default model**, so `F 2` cannot fall back to LogUp by omission; `BalanceModel.Reads model Ch` ties each model to the channel kind it reads, and the Layer 3 builders take typed channels through it |

Why a tag in the message and not a new field: adding a field to `Interaction`/`AbstractInteraction` breaks every anonymous constructor downstream (sp1-lean); deriving direction from `assumeGuarantees` reclassifies legacy `emit (-1)` as a provider (rejected, #16 item 1 and blueprint B6); a separate raw channel per direction breaks channel identity. The tag survives construction, subcircuit composition, evaluation, collection and JSON export without touching any public record; one fixture carries it through a nested subcircuit to the collected interactions, and the exported JSON is pinned by `#guard`.

`BalanceModel` is an **abstract count/support interface**: its `view` (the reading of interactions as events) is supplied by the model and nothing in the structure ties it to the raw channel contract. A model is usable in a channel soundness argument only with a separately proved **correspondence law** for the encoding it reads (A17): the view recovers payload, direction and activity of every evaluated interaction; the argument is applied per raw channel; permission stays with `assumeGuarantees`; pull support transports the provider's requirement to the receiver's guarantee.

Priorities, in order: zero source changes for legacy users (an acceptance criterion, not an assumption); every hypothesis kept only with a proved counterexample to the statement without it; every commit green under `lake build --wfail` and `lake build CleanTests`; landed proofs only (no `sorry`, `axiom`, `native_decide`).

## Layer checklist

The single Clean pull request #464 carries every layer, so a layer is ticked when the commit implementing it is on the pull request branch; the line records the commit and its review state. Merging the pull request closes this issue.

- [x] **Layer 0 — compatibility boundary, tag representation, model-aware wrapper.** `Direction`, `DirectedChannel`, `DirectedChannel.toRaw` (raw requirements: boolean gate ∧ well-formed tag ∧ active-provider guarantee), `DirectedInteraction` and its five constructors, the typed `Guarantees`/`Requirements` with `toRaw_guarantees`/`toRaw_requirements`, the five circuit ops with `ExplicitCircuits` instances, `emittedValue`, `eval_toRaw`; the kernel views `Event`, `PullsSupported`, `activeCount`, `CountBalanced` (definitions only); `BalanceModel` (documented as an abstract interface), `Balanced`, `BalancedChannelsWith`, `StatementWith`, `SoundnessWith`, `CompletenessWith`, `FormalEnsembleWith`; fixtures A1, A11, A13, A14, the Layer 0 half of A17 (malformed tag rejected; `blindModel`), A18 (`nestedProto`), the JSON shape and identical-bytes pins, the `proto` circuit and the three legacy `F 2` theorems (`legacy_length_le_one_over_F2`, `legacyProto_satisfiable`, `legacyProto_only_empty`). **On #464:** [`dbc16bf4`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/dbc16bf4) (adversarially reviewed 2026-09-15: no false theorem, hole, axiom or legacy change; findings F1–F3) and [`3f0996bd`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/3f0996bd) (the review follow-up; **awaiting review**).
- [x] **Layer 1 — shared mathematical kernel and legacy bridges.** `guarantees_of_requirements_of_count_eq`, `pullsSupported_of_countBalanced`, `countBalanced_of_perm_activePayloads`, `activePayloads`, `Interaction.legacyEvent`, `pullsSupported_legacyEvent_of_balancedInteractions`, `countBalanced_legacyEvent_of_balancedInteractions`, `count_eq_of_balancedInteractions`; the legacy VM theorem keeps its name and binders and delegates its induction to the kernel (its `[Fact (ringChar F ≠ 2)]` binder, provably redundant, was removed on 2026-09-18 together with the binders of the VM builder: the one deliberate departure from byte-identical legacy signatures). `BalanceModel.logUp` (`= BalancedInteractions` by `Iff.rfl`), `BalanceModel.multiset`, `Interaction.directedEvent`, `DirectedChannel.directedEvent_emittedValue` and `DirectedChannel.guarantees_of_requirements_of_pullsSupported` (the directed correspondence law, A17), the `_iff_…_logUp` theorems (all `Iff.rfl`), `FormalEnsemble.withLogUp`; the law packaged as `RawChannel.ConsistentWith model` with `consistent_iff_consistentWith_logUp`, instances for the two supported pairings only, and the field `FormalEnsembleWith.consistent` (decided 2026-09-18); `BalanceModel.Reads model Ch`, the static model/channel tie, with instances for `logUp`/`Channel` and `multiset`/`DirectedChannel` only and the `circuit_norm` erasure lemmas (decided 2026-09-21); tests A2–A6, A14, A15 over a channel with an arbitrary guarantee, the A17 reading tests, the mismatched-pairing tests in both directions (`legacy_not_consistentWith_multiset` false, `directed_consistentWith_logUp` true but vacuous), the four `#check_failure` pins and `transport_needs_support`. **On #464:** [`7b4d4a2a`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/7b4d4a2a) (kernel and legacy bridges), [`a70a6f9a`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/a70a6f9a) (models and directed reading), [`83f28efb`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/83f28efb) (A17 reading tests): reviewed 2026-09-17 by an independent agent (no false theorem, hole, axiom or legacy change; two major and seven minor findings, all answered); [`0f00cf91`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/0f00cf91) (review follow-up: `ConsistentWith`, load-bearing A15, fixtures, proof cleanup) and [`bc0de6d8`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/bc0de6d8) (removal of the redundant characteristic assumption): both reviewed 2026-09-18 (`doc/roadmap/bus-balance-review-bc0de6d8.md`: axioms clean, no legacy change beyond the recorded binder removal, every kernel hypothesis with a compiled counterexample; one major finding, `RawChannel.ConsistentWith (.logUp F)` is provable for every directed channel, and two minor); [`ecba22d1`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/ecba22d1) (review follow-up 3: `BalanceModel.Reads` as the static tie, corrected docstrings, `directed_consistentWith_logUp`, the `#check_failure` pins, `transport_needs_support`, `Balance.lean` module map): **awaiting review**.
- [x] **Layer 2 — opt-in directed local contract.** `emittedValue_guarantees_iff`, `emittedValue_requirements_iff`, the eight operation-by-operation lemmas (`pushedIf_requirements_iff`, `pushedIf_guarantees`, `pulledIf_guarantees_iff`, `pulledIf_requirements_iff`, `emitted_receive_guarantees`, `emitted_receive_requirements_iff`, `guarantees_of_enabled_eq_zero`, `requirements_of_enabled_eq_zero`), `toRaw_inj`, `expose`; tests A7, A8, A12 and the directed weight-2 rejection. **On #464:** [`e0be7dca`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/e0be7dca) (the cherry-pick of `522ed6d2` onto the roadmap commit, 2026-09-21, pushed 2026-09-22; `lake build --wfail`, `lake build CleanTests` and `#print axioms` green): **awaiting review**.
- [x] **Layer 3 — models through ensemble soundness.** What landed (2026-09-22): the kernel count adapter `Event.key`, `perm_activePayloads_of_countBalanced`, `count_eq_of_countBalanced`; `BalanceModel.multiset.UnitEvent` as the boolean-gate discipline (decided 2026-09-18; it changes nothing the model accepts); the directed VM theorem `DirectedChannel.guarantees_of_requirements_of_requirements_of_guarantees` as an instance of the kernel, over any field; `Clean/Air/OrderedChannelWith.lean` (`PartialBalancedChannelWith`, `SoundChannelsWith`, `TableSoundnessWith`, `SoundEnsembleWith` with the typed gate `addChannel`/`addFinishedChannel (channel : Ch Message) [model.Reads Ch]` erasing through `Reads.toRaw`, the raw escape hatches `addRawChannel`/`addFinishedRawChannel [channel.ConsistentWith model]`, `markFinished` owing only membership, `toFormal` filling `FormalEnsembleWith.consistent` from the record's `channels_consistent` (consistency carried for every channel, gate where the channel is added; decided 2026-09-23, blueprint amended), the pointwise bridges to the legacy record, and the module docstring on where #452's capacity premise enters); `Clean/Air/VmWith.lean` (`DirectedVmTables`, `SoundVmChannelWith`, `SoundVmEnsembleWith` with `toFormal`, `Ensemble.addDirectedVm`, the witness-level directed VM theorem obtaining count balance through `countBalanced_of_balanced` with the gates from the row constraints, `SoundEnsembleWith.addVm` for the multiset model; one model per ensemble); tests: the typed gate pinned in both directions and through the raw entry, an ordered ensemble closed under the multiset model with a nonempty `F 2` witness, a counter VM through `addVm` and `toFormal` with a nonempty `F 2` witness, necessity fixtures for every hypothesis of the count adapter and the directed VM theorem (`pushes_provide` kept as the one recorded exception). `CompletenessWith` exists since Layer 0; no completeness theorem is proved. **On #464:** [`78e750f2`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/78e750f2) (kernel and models), [`314a6523`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/314a6523) (ordered channels and builders), [`e25bce70`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/e25bce70) (directed VM), [`51839b7c`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/51839b7c) (tests, README): reviewed 2026-09-23 by an independent agent (`doc/roadmap/bus-balance-review-51839b7c.md`: no false theorem, hole, axiom or legacy change; two major, three minor, five nits, all answered); [`8b54acbd`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/8b54acbd) (review follow-up: corrected `pushes_provide` fixture, nonempty VM witness, redundant binder dropped, escape-hatch docstrings, fixture dedup): **awaiting review**. Deferred (user's call): the ordered-channel induction is duplicated in the model-aware file rather than derived, since deriving it needs `OrderedChannel.lean` split into definitions and theorems.
- [x] **Layer 4 — useful binary-field behavior.** What landed: first a counter VM over a binary field (2026-09-23, [`7875acf9`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/7875acf9), [`0a41e630`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/0a41e630); reviewed adversarially, no critical or major finding), then, because its diagonal state (accumulator = program counter) made the fixed-step result trivially field-independent, the Fibonacci VM that replaced it on 2026-09-24 ([`286ebf17`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/286ebf17)): `Clean/Examples/FibonacciWithDirectedChannels.lean`, the directed twin of `Clean/Examples/FibonacciWithChannels.lean`. State channel `FibChannel` with the guarantee `(x, y) = (fib n, fib (n + 1))` for some `n : ℕ` read into the field, an addition lookup channel `AddChannel`, the gated step `fibStep`, the verifier `fibVerifier N` (provides `(0, 0, 1)`, receives the state at index `N`), `fibVm N` and `fibEnsemble N` under the multiset model. Theorems, all on the three standard axioms: `fibEnsemble_soundness` (over any field, the output is `(fib k, fib (k + 1))` for some `k` with `(k : F) = N`, so `N` fixes the index modulo the characteristic, the same shape as the legacy `fibonacci_soundness`; a non-diagonal accumulator has no `output = N` analogue over a general field); `fibEnsemble_rejects_zero` (the output `(0, 0)` is rejected over every field and every `N`, since consecutive Fibonacci numbers are coprime); `fibEnsemble_one_step_over_F2` (`N = 1`, output `(1, 1)`, four interactions on the state channel and two on the addition channel); `fibEnsemble_three_steps_over_F2` (the same `N = 1` accepts the run `0 → 1 → 0 → 1` with output `(0, 1)`: the statement admits two outputs over `F 2`); `legacy_rejects_every_run` (the legacy relation admits no witness of the ensemble over `F 2`, whatever `N`). A9 and A10 are met in that form. The two fixture files stay in `Clean/Air/Test/`; the example is built with the library. Awaits the user's review.
- [ ] **Layer 5 — document and validate adoption.** Landed 2026-09-23: the bus export protocol, version 1 ([`20e77970`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/20e77970): `Clean/Air/BusProtocol.lean`, `ChannelSchema`, `BusProtocol` with protocol name `clean-bus` and version `1`, `BalanceModel.Protocol`, one lemma per clause, pinned by `#guard`; the discriminator sits outside the per-interaction JSON, whose bytes are unchanged), and the README section on the legacy and directed channel contracts, the backend relations and the export protocol ([`8da2375f`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/8da2375f); compressed with the rest of the README in [`a1938ad5`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/a1938ad5)). Open: A16, the representative leanerVM integration with its observed migration cost, which is a separate pull request by another agent. Awaits the user's review.

Ordering: 0 first; 1 and 2 need 0 and are independent of each other; 3 needs 1 and 2; 4 needs 3; 5 needs 4.

## Acceptance tests

From the roadmap's table; evidence is in `Clean/Air/Test/BusBalance.lean` unless noted.

| ID | Required evidence | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | `(-1 : F 2) = 1`; the tag still distinguishes a provider from a receive | Layer 0: over `F 2` and over every field, plus the directed JSON serialization-shape pin |
| A2 | field-sum balance without the guard admits two unsupported unit receives over `F 2` | Layer 1: `logUp_guard_necessary` |
| A3 | directed multiset balance rejects two providers with no receive | Layer 1: `multiset_rejects_two_providers` |
| A4 | unrestricted signed receive weights can invalidate LogUp-derived pull support | **adapted, for review:** under the sign reading a weight `-2` is a provider, not a receive (`legacy_reads_weight_two_receive_as_provider`, over `F 5` where `-2` is neither `1` nor `-1`, Layer 1); the directed path rejects any non-unit gate locally (Layer 2, `e0be7dca`) |
| A5 | unrestricted signed receive weights can invalidate unit-event count equality | Layer 1: `logUp_unit_receives_necessary` (a weight-2 receive against two unit providers is LogUp-balanced, reads as a provider, and breaks count balance) |
| A6 | weight-2 provider and two unit receives: LogUp-balanced, unequal operation counts | Layer 1: `logUp_unit_events_necessary` |
| A7 | the kernel's provider-role hypothesis is necessary | Layer 2 (`e0be7dca`): `bridge_provider_role_necessary`; Layer 3: `pull_role_necessary`, `balance_necessary`, `pushes_channel_necessary`, `pulls_channel_necessary` for the directed VM theorem, and `count_eq_len_necessary`, `count_eq_pulls_receive_necessary`, `count_eq_pushes_provide_necessary` for the count adapter (the last corrected in review) |
| A8 | the kernel's activity hypothesis is necessary | Layer 2 (`e0be7dca`): `bridge_activity_necessary` |
| A9 | explicit nonempty binary-field ensemble witness with per-channel counts | Layer 4: `fibEnsemble_one_step_over_F2` (four interactions on the state channel, two on the addition channel) and `fibEnsemble_three_steps_over_F2` (eight and six), both over `F 2`; in miniature at ensemble level in Layer 3: `oneEnsemble_statement_over_F2` and `counterEnsemble_statement_over_F2` (a two-interaction list miniature exists in Layer 1: `multiset_accepts_matched_pair` vs `logUp_rejects_matched_pair`) |
| A10 | the directed VM/ensemble chain proves the fixed-step result and rejects the wrong output | Layer 4: `fibEnsemble_soundness` (the fixed-step result, modular in the characteristic) and `fibEnsemble_rejects_zero` (the output `(0, 0)`, over every field and every `N`); `legacy_rejects_every_run` for the legacy side |
| A11 | legacy `emit (-1)` neither assumes nor owes, even a `False` guarantee | Layer 0 |
| A12 | active provider owes; receiver may assume or decline; disabled events owe nothing | Layer 2 (`e0be7dca`) |
| A13 | existing constructor syntax, two-premise proof shape, theorem calls, metadata, JSON unchanged | Layer 0: pinned signatures of `exists_push_of_pull`, `one_ne_neg_one`, the legacy VM theorem (pin amended 2026-09-18 when its redundant `[Fact (ringChar F ≠ 2)]` binder was removed; callers relying on instance synthesis still elaborate); legacy JSON `#guard`; the Fibonacci example, `OrderedChannel.lean` and `Vm.lean` build unchanged. sp1-lean itself not built: **unverified** beyond the fixtures |
| A14 | explicit model over a generic field, no default instance, survives every builder; `F 2` never falls back to LogUp | Layer 0 (abstract model; the `Prop`-valued examples are typechecking tests and labelled as such), Layer 1 (`.multiset`); Layer 3: the model survives every builder and conversion (`oneEnsemble`, `oneFormal`, `counterEnsemble` over any field, instantiated at `F 2`), and the typed gate is pinned in both directions and through the raw entry |
| A15 | both adapters feed the shared support/count proofs; no unproved coercion between weights and counts | Layer 1, in miniature over a channel with an arbitrary guarantee `P`: the receive's guarantee is `P 1`, the pair's requirements are `P 1`, and the multiset balance feeds the `ConsistentWith` instance to transport one to the other (the docstring says this is `P 1 → P 1` once unfolded and what it evidences); `transport_needs_support` shows the transport theorem's pull-support hypothesis is load-bearing; full chain in Layer 3: `oneEnsemble_tableSoundness` (multiset balance feeds the channel's consistency, which transports the provider's requirement to the consumer's guarantee) and the directed VM chain through `countBalanced_of_balanced` and the directed VM theorem (`VmWith.lean`) |
| A16 | a representative leanerVM consumer uses the new relation with no characteristic restriction | Layer 5, open: a separate leanerVM pull request by another agent |
| A17 | correspondence law for each reading a model uses (recovery of payload/direction/activity, per-channel application, permission unchanged, requirement-to-guarantee transport), tested on malformed tags and actual activity | Layer 0: the raw contract rejects malformed tags (`#v[0, 2]` fails for every gate); `blindModel` shows the structure alone does not imply the law. Layer 1: `directedEvent_emittedValue`, `guarantees_of_requirements_of_pullsSupported`, the two reading tests (a malformed tag reads as an active receive that assumes nothing and fails the contract; a disabled interaction is not an active event), and the law packaged as `RawChannel.ConsistentWith` tested on a mismatched pairing in both directions: false for the multiset model on a legacy channel (`multiset_accepts_two_legacy_pulls`, `legacy_not_consistentWith_multiset`), true but vacuous for the LogUp model on a directed channel (`logUp_rejects_directed_pair`, `directed_consistentWith_logUp`); instance search declares neither mismatch (`#check_failure` pins); the static tie `BalanceModel.Reads` pinned in both directions |
| A18 | one fixture carries the representation through nested subcircuit, flattening, evaluation and collection | Layer 0: `nestedProto` |
| A19 | the directed export identifies its interpretation | Layer 5 ([`20e77970`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/20e77970)): `BusProtocol` binds the protocol name and version, the balance model, tag removal before opposite directions are compared, and the gate and malformed-tag handling, each pinned by `#guard`; the per-interaction JSON bytes are unchanged and the identical-bytes fact against a legacy two-element payload stays pinned (Layer 0) |
| legacy `F 2` facts | what the legacy relation does and does not exclude over `F 2` | Layer 0: at most one interaction per channel (`legacy_length_le_one_over_F2`); the legacy prototype statement is satisfied by the empty witness (`legacyProto_satisfiable`) and only by empty prototype tables (`legacyProto_only_empty`) |

## Frontier

- **Where we sit (2026-09-24).** Layers 4 and 5 (without A16) are on #464, pushed 2026-09-24, head [`a1938ad5`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/a1938ad5). The safekeeping commits were dropped and the branch history rewritten, so every hash quoted in this issue for commits after [`ecba22d1`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/ecba22d1) refers to the old history; the current ones are Layer 2 [`ee0b84ac`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/ee0b84ac); Layer 3 [`c2fd237c`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/c2fd237c), [`016bdcd9`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/016bdcd9), [`711efa8b`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/711efa8b), [`dee89263`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/dee89263) and its follow-up [`1f81d475`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/1f81d475); Layer 5 [`20e77970`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/20e77970), [`8da2375f`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/8da2375f); Layer 4 [`7875acf9`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/7875acf9), [`0a41e630`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/0a41e630), the Fibonacci example [`286ebf17`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/286ebf17); and the comment-style commit [`a1938ad5`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/a1938ad5) (comment-only: every module doc and docstring of the change shortened to the library's style and every reference to this roadmap, its layers, acceptance labels, decisions and review history removed; the comment-stripped sources are byte-identical). Awaiting the user's review: Layers 2, 4 and 5 and the two 2026-09-24 commits. Open items are unchanged: decision 16 (the gate source), the deferred ordered-channel induction duplication, and A16.
- **Where we sit (2026-09-23).** Layers 2 and 3 are on #464 (pushed 2026-09-23, head [`d85738dd`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/commit/d85738dd)). Layer 2 is the cherry-pick `e0be7dca` and awaits review. Layer 3 landed 2026-09-22 in four commits, was audited for a domain reader (headliners: `SoundEnsembleWith` and its builders, `toFormal`, `DirectedVmTables`, `addVm`, the directed VM theorem, the `UnitEvent` change) and reviewed adversarially on 2026-09-23 (`doc/roadmap/bus-balance-review-51839b7c.md`): no false theorem, hole, axiom or legacy change; two major findings (a necessity fixture that dropped two hypotheses at once; no satisfiability witness for the VM bundle), three minor (a redundant binder; `SoundEnsemble.withLogUp` as an undocumented third route to the vacuous pairing; the ordered-channel induction duplicated rather than derived), five nits; all answered in `8b54acbd` except the duplication, which is deferred. Decisions taken 2026-09-23 from the audit: the consistency gate sits where a channel is added (`addChannel` via `Reads`, `addRawChannel` via the instance; `markFinished` owes membership only; blueprint amended); one model per ensemble (pending decision 6 closed); `pushes_provide` on the list-level directed VM theorem kept as the one recorded exception to the counterexample rule (the statement holds without it by a global count that is not the kernel's induction; the count adapter needs it). Under LogUp every directed gate is `0` or `1` and nothing cancels, so a balanced, requirement-satisfying list has no active interaction and every directed guarantee holds with a false premise. The docstrings had said the obligation "cannot be supplied" for a mismatched pairing; that is true for the multiset model on a legacy channel (the obligation is false there) and false for the LogUp model on a directed channel, which is precisely the pairing whose statement is met only by inactive traces and whose soundness is vacuous. ## How to work on this

- **Claim a slice:** open an issue titled `[Intention]: Clean bus: Layer N: …` listing the exact declaration names taken, link it here, close it when the layer's commit lands on Clean #464.
- **Report a problem with the roadmap:** open `[Roadmap]: Clean bus: …` naming the layer and the acceptance item or compatibility rule it touches.
- **Change the roadmap:** a pull request editing the roadmap file, titled `docs(bus-balance): …`, referencing this issue. A commit that lands a layer on #464 rewrites the status file whole and ticks the layer above with the commit link.
- **Review, one layer per pass.** Statement reviewed independently of proof; every hypothesis in a new theorem justified by a counterexample to the statement without it, else flagged for manual review; every proposed change to an existing declaration shown beside the old one; legacy public statements byte-identical (`exists_push_of_pull`, `one_ne_neg_one`, `RawChannel.Normal/Consistent`, the VM theorem (minus its `[Fact (ringChar F ≠ 2)]` binder, removed 2026-09-18 as the one recorded exception), `Statement`, `FormalEnsemble`, the builders, the JSON of existing interactions); no edits proposed to sp1-lean. Review findings are answered by a separate follow-up commit on #464 so the response is auditable on its own.
- **Per Clean commit:** `lake build --wfail` and `lake build CleanTests` green, `scripts/check-consecutive-empty-lines.py` clean; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `unsafe`, `native_decide`.
- **Closing this issue:** Clean #464 implementing Layers 0–5 has merged, leanerVM's Clean pin is bumped to it, #16 is closed by that bump, and leanISA Layer 9's block comments (#4) are theorems.
